thread:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: High error rate and latency on /v1/generate in us-west-2. Pager triggered for oncall-sre. Summary: packet retransmits on IB fabric + some runtime pods OOMing. Auto-fallback attempted but some requests are 503ing.

oncall-bot: Pagerduty: Alert PAGER-9321 -> Jun (sre) has been notified. Severity: Sev2.

Jun: I'm on it. Pulling logs and checking cluster health. Anyone on network? @Raj?

Raj: here. I see spikes in IB retransmit counters on rack-12. Quick glance at host-level `ifstat` and `ibstat` shows link up but high retry.

Raj: paste: ```
# ibstat rxe0
CA 'mlx5_0'
  CA type: MT4105
  Number of ports: 1
  Port 1:
    State: ACTIVE
    Physical state: LinkUp
    Rate: 100Gb/sec (4X)
```

Raj: and kernel dmesg snippet: ```
[  1234.567890] mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: VNIC reset due to event 0x8
[  1234.568010] mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: MCQ error: FLR
[  1250.789012] ib_retry_exceeded on mlx5_0, qp 34567
```

Amy: I'm seeing a surge of 500s in the app logs and some containers in `serving-prod` namespace restarting. Example from k8s events: `Back-off restarting failed container` on `runtime-xyz-pod-2`.

Matt: checking runtime side. `nvidia-smi` on node shows a few processes at 98-100% memory, and host OOM killer activity. Some worker containers got SIGKILL.

Matt: `kubectl -n serving-prod describe pod runtime-xyz-pod-2` shows CrashLoopBackOff with reason OOMKilled.

Jun: So we have correlated symptoms: intermittent IB packet loss/retransmits leading to higher latencies, which increases model sequence lengths and KV cache growth => some pods use more GPU memory and OOM. Need parallel network + runtime mitigations.

Raj: Actions I'm going to try now: 1) reduce RDMA offload that triggers path MTU frag for a subset of NICs, 2) check for recent MTU config drift, 3) throttle east-west calls from that rack to limit retransmit amplification.

Raj: Running quick check for MTU mismatches: ```
# ip link show dev eth0
3: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
# ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
large_receive_offload: on
```

Raj: I also see ECN marking spikes on the ToR -> will try disabling ECN on the host to reduce retransmit storms.

Matt: From runtime: I'll start draining the worst nodes and restart pods onto healthier nodes. Also will enable KV cache TTL reduction for affected model to shrink memory footprint: bump `kv_cache_ttl_ms` from `600000` -> `60000` for canary.

Matt: Quick mitigation commands I will run: ```
# cordon node rack-12-node-07
kubectl cordon rack-12-node-07
# drain (evict pods gracefully)
kubectl drain rack-12-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Amy: I've opened a narrow rule in the routing layer to send traffic for `prod-generate` to other racks as a temporary failover and reduce load on rack-12. Rolling out now.

Eli: Support note: customer telemetry shows 12 customers with 10-30% increased error rates; top affected product is streaming chat in us-west-2. CS notified and we sent an automated status update.

Katie: Product asked for a short blameless summary for customers: estimate impact window and whether data loss occurred. We don't think requests were dropped (some got 503s), no PII exposure. Keep me posted.

Jun: Handing network path to Raj and runtime to Matt. I'll sit on coordination and customer comms. If either team needs escalation, ping me with `@Jun` and `urgency:high`.

Raj: I've disabled ECN on the nodes in rack-12 and temporarily lowered NIC LRO/GRO to reduce fragmentation. Commands: ```
ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off gso off
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_ecn=0
```

Raj: After the change retransmit counters started to fall from 1200/min -> ~200/min on the affected hosts. Still seeing occasional qp retries.

Matt: After draining the two worst nodes and restarting pods, OOM events dropped. I also applied a hotfix to the runtime to reduce batch size on high-latency requests: set `max_batch_tokens: 1024` -> `512` for rollout group.

Matt: Also proactively scaled up a small CPU fallback pool for tiny requests to avoid GPU hits while we stabilize.

Amy: Traffic re-route completed. Errors on /v1/generate dropped by ~60% in the last 6 minutes. Latency p95 improving.

Eli: CS update: initial status posted. Several customers asked for ETA — ETA TBD. We told them we're mitigating network issue and reducing load; will provide a 1 hour update.

Jun: Good progress. Two open items: 1) root cause for RDMA retransmit (hardware vs driver vs config), 2) follow-up to prevent memory spikes under degraded network. Raj/Matt please state follow-up owners.

Raj: I'll open a post-incident ticket to run NIC firmware checks, review ToR counters, and double-check MTU consistency across the rack. Owner: Raj (network).

Matt: I'll own the runtime follow-ups: add a defensive memory-cgroup for runtime containers, add adaptive batch throttling under high-retransmit signals, and expand KV cache autoshrink. Owner: Matt (runtime).

Jun: Oncall handoff in 20m to Amy. Amy you'll be primary then — I'll keep monitoring.

Amy: ack. I'll take primary at +20. I've synced with CS and infra.

Jun: Quick recap for postmortem notes: timeline: 1719002468 alert -> IB retransmit spike -> container OOMs -> routing failover and node drains -> ECN disable + NIC LRO/GRO off -> pod restarts + batch throttling -> errors down and p95 improving.

Eli: Customers asking if dedicated deployments were affected. Amy: were any dedicated instances impacted?

Amy: Dedicated customers on the same rack had brief increased latency but no sustained 503s; we flagged account teams to proactively reach out for any concerns.

Raj: I'm scheduling ToR level packet captures for post-incident (pcap) and will coordinate with hardware vendor if we see CRCs or parity errors.

Matt: I'll push a canary config change to prod to make the batch size adaptive on signal `network_retransmit_rate > 1000/min` to preempt memory growth.

oncall-bot: Reminder: On-call rotation handoff scheduled in 20 minutes. Please ensure notes are in the incident doc and handoff message is posted.

Jun: Marking this as "mitigated" for now — services stabilizing. We'll keep it open for postmortem and follow-ups. If we see another spike, escalate to Sev1 and re-pager.

Amy: taking handoff now. I'll post a short incident summary to #incidents and link to postmortem ticket. :thumbsup:

Eli: I'll update the customer status page with current mitigation and next update time.

Jun: Thanks team. Postmortem owners: Raj + Matt + Amy. Close when follow-ups are assigned and customer comms complete.

Amy: created ticket INFRA-4512 and assigned to Raj/Matt. Closing the live thread but keeping it referenced for the postmortem.

infra-bot: Incident changed: severity -> mitigated. Metrics back to baseline.

Jun: closing thread. :white_check_mark:
